summary: Hegemony casts each player as a distinct social class (Workers, Capitalists, Middle Class, or the State) with wildly asymmetric goals and mechanisms, all fighting over a shared national economy through legislation, production, and negotiation. It plays like a economic simulation crossed with a political board game, where policy votes and class interests genuinely put players at odds.
praised: genuinely asymmetric factions with different win conditions
sharp systemic commentary on economics baked into mechanics
high replayability from shifting alliances and legislation
rewards real negotiation and reading the table
criticised: very high complexity and rules overhead
long playtime that can drag for less-engaged players
steep learning curve requiring a patient first game
some feel it lectures rather than simulates

interaction.kind: asymmetric class economy with voting and direct exploitation
interaction.detail: Working-class laborers are employed in buildings built by capitalist players, so wages and conditions set by one player directly affect another's income, and strikes or state policy can hit an opponent's engine directly. All classes buy and sell through a shared commodity market and vote on the same national policy board, with real negotiation and lobbying over how votes go, not just parallel building.

scoring.how_you_win: Each player plays a different class with its own success metric (e.g. worker welfare vs. capitalist profit vs. state stability); whoever best advances their own class's agenda relative to its targets by game end wins.

_name: Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory
